headline: Inflation breaks 6 percent as foreign money floods back

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Sunday, the fifteenth of November, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most this morning. First, inflation. Retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent in October, crossing the Reserve Bank's upper tolerance limit of 6 percent. Economists now expect it to stay above that line for a few months, and that strengthens the case for another rate hike in December.

Second, foreign money is pouring back. Foreign portfolio investors have put more than 76,000 crore rupees into Indian shares so far this month, and a monthly record is in sight.

And third, the primary market wakes up. Three public issues worth over 10,000 crore rupees open this week, led by Coal India's subsidiary, Mahanadi Coalfields.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Now to how markets closed on Friday. The Sensex fell about 319 points to 81,592, and the Nifty dropped 155 points to 25,144. That ended a three-session rally, as the inflation number spooked traders. Still, both indices finished the week up, by somewhere between 0.7 and 1.3 percent.

Step back, and the picture is one of a comeback. The MSCI India index has rebounded 11 percent from its six-month low in October, adding more than 400 billion dollars in value and almost erasing this year's losses. The trade is being called a great rotation. As global investors pull back from artificial intelligence stocks, India's relative lack of AI exposure has turned into an advantage. A senior government official said some of that money could reach India through foreign institutional investors, and could even help Indian IT services companies.

On flows, foreign investors have now put in more than 76,000 crore rupees in November, after pulling out about 70,700 crore rupees across September and October.

Two stock moves stood out. Paytm crossed its November 2021 listing price of 1,950 rupees for the first time in nearly five years, touching 1,960 before closing at 1,934, after the Reserve Bank gave in-principle approval for its wallet business. And PB Fintech rose nearly 5 percent on a report that the insurance regulator may rework its draft paper on distribution.

Now the levels to watch. Sudeep Shah of SBI Securities says the bullish bias stays intact as long as the Nifty holds the 24,800 support zone. A Moneycontrol technical view warns that a break below 25,000 could extend profit booking, while a move above the recent swing high of 25,425 could trigger a sharp rally. Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi sees the next big resistance at 25,500 to 25,600. Further out, Sandeep Daga of Nine Rivers Capital thinks a retest of the old high near 26,373 is achievable in the coming months.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
To the primary market, where a busy week lies ahead. The big one is Mahanadi Coalfields, which opens on Thursday, the nineteenth. It's a pure offer for sale, with Coal India selling up to 66.18 crore shares, or 10 percent of the company, so none of the money goes to Mahanadi itself. The issue is estimated at around 9,500 crore rupees, roughly a billion dollars. The company produced about 218 million tonnes of coal last financial year, and its grey market premium was quoted at 12.5 rupees a share.

Before that, Crystal Crop Protection opens on Wednesday, the eighteenth, with a grey market premium of nearly 17 percent. A smaller SME issue, Watrana Rentals, completes the list.

Further down the pipeline, SEBI has cleared Sembcorp Green Infra, Razorpay and MakeMyTrip to go public.

On deals, SoftBank sold 1.65 percent of Meesho for 1,885 crore rupees to 16 buyers. Fidelity was the biggest, picking up half a percent for about 573 crore rupees. In IIFL Capital Services, three investors, Alpha Alternatives, Neo Group and Arvesta Financial, together sold a 1.69 percent stake for over 224 crore rupees. And a setback for VA Tech Wabag: the Saudi Water Authority has cancelled its Yanbu desalination project, worth about 2,400 crore rupees, citing internal reasons.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
A quick results roundup, as the September quarter season winds down.

In industrials, RHI Magnesita's net profit jumped 62 percent to about 62 crore rupees, on revenue of around 1,038 crore rupees, with operating profit up 30 percent as costs fell. NMDC disappointed. Its operating profit slipped 3 percent to about 1,940 crore rupees, below expectations, and the stock fell nearly 2 percent to just under 70 rupees.

In media and entertainment, Prime Focus, the parent of the visual effects firm behind the Ramayana film, posted a more than fourteen-fold jump in net profit to about 58 crore rupees, as revenue grew 35 percent to around 1,410 crore rupees.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy, and back to that inflation number. Retail inflation rose for the ninth month in a row, to 6.09 percent in October from 5.54 percent in September. Food inflation hit 8.94 percent, and onion prices were up a startling 116 percent. Six states crossed 7 percent, including four in the south, while poorer states like Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh saw the sharpest climb since April. The pressure is spreading beyond food, too. Inflation in mobile phones rose to 8.65 percent, and in laptops and tablets to 8.61 percent. A Moneycontrol analysis finds 95 of 358 items running above 6 percent.

On trade, October brought record exports but a wider gap. Merchandise exports jumped 45 percent to a record 49.47 billion dollars, but imports surged to 89.35 billion, pushing the trade deficit to a one-year high of 39.88 billion dollars, up from about 30 billion in September.

On growth, SBI Research expects the economy to have grown 7.8 percent in the September quarter, above the Reserve Bank's estimate of 7.2 percent.

In policy, the Cabinet approved a rabi fertiliser subsidy of 62,370 crore rupees, up 64 percent, while keeping di-ammonium phosphate at 1,350 rupees a bag despite rising global prices. It also cleared 5,000 crore rupees for a MUDRA credit guarantee fund. Looking ahead to the Budget, industry bodies are asking for a cut in long-term capital gains tax.

One for the profession: the Bombay Chartered Accountants' Society has urged SEBI to let CA firms monitor how money raised in smaller issues is used, and to make monitoring agencies flag related-party payments and spending outside the stated objects.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, the story of the week has been Nvidia. News of an affair involving chief executive Jensen Huang sent the shares tumbling, wiping roughly 2 trillion dollars off the chipmaker's value in a week. On Friday, Nvidia fell another 4 percent and AMD dropped nearly 10 percent, dragging Wall Street lower, while sticky inflation kept bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike alive.

Microsoft had its own trouble, a global outage of more than 24 hours that hit Outlook and Teams in over 70 countries. It ruled out a cyberattack.

Crypto is under heavy pressure. Bitcoin fell 5.7 percent on Saturday and kept sliding in Asia this morning, to as low as around 62,000 dollars, its weakest in about four months, as leveraged bets were wiped out.

The coming week brings minutes of the last Fed meeting, Nvidia's earnings, and continuing risks around Iran, all of which commodity markets are watching closely.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the India and US trade deal you're following. On Saturday, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said the two sides have sorted out the bulk of the issues and the deal could be sealed soon. He said the talks are at the finishing line, and that much of what remains is on the American side. That comes about a month before Prime Minister Modi's likely visit to the US for the G20 Summit, where he may meet President Trump.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, starting with a few rulings worth knowing. The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted a 3.69 crore rupee addition against a woman who had routed payments between bangle traders through her account, holding that those deposits were not automatically her income. The Jammu and Kashmir High Court barred a bank from recovering someone else's loan from a retired guarantor's pension account, though another High Court has taken a different view. And the Supreme Court held that a son cannot automatically claim a share in his grandfather's property once a partition has made his father its exclusive owner.

One date for your calendar: the window to disclose unreported foreign assets and income under the FAST-DS 2026 scheme, using Form 1, closes on the thirty-first of December.

For savers, the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme pays 8.2 percent this quarter, with a ceiling of 30 lakh rupees, while Kisan Vikas Patra pays 7.5 percent and matures in 115 months, with no upper limit.

Two cautions. Technology funds are the worst-performing equity category this year, down about 10.5 percent. And Indian investors in US exchange-traded funds that trade at steep premiums could lose money even if the underlying shares hold steady. SEBI's chairman, Mr Pandey, also urged India's more than 15 crore investors to understand products and weigh the risks before investing.

That's the brief. Tomorrow, watch how markets digest the inflation number after Friday's dip, and whether the Nifty holds 25,000. Crystal Crop Protection opens on Wednesday and Mahanadi Coalfields on Thursday, with wholesale inflation, the Fed minutes and Nvidia's results due through the week. Have a restful Sunday, and I'll be back with you tomorrow morning.
